The yellowing appears diffuse. Top candidates: Leaf_Mold, Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus, Verticillium_Wilt, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus.

Now viewing one reference from each top candidate class:
Excellent match! The Leaf_Mold reference (CDDM_3196) very closely resembles the test image - same gray background, single leaf, yellow-green diffuse patches. Let me verify with a few more classes.

All 8 reference views used across 8 different classes. Summary of findings:

- **Leaf_Mold (CDDM_3196)**: Near-identical match — same gray concrete background, single elongated leaf, diffuse yellow-green patches in same distribution pattern. Very strong visual match.
- **Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus**: Shows severely distorted/curled leaves with mosaic — leaf shape distortion doesn't match.
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: Whole plant wilting with pale leaves — doesn't match single leaf with yellow patches.
- **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus**: Whole plant bronzing/wilting — no match.
- **Powdery_Mildew**: White powdery coating — completely different.
- **Early_Blight**: Dark concentric ring lesions — completely different.
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**: Small circular dark spots — completely different.
- **Leaf_Mold (CDDM_313)**: Also shows pale patches on leaf upper surface consistent with Leaf Mold.

The test image shows classic Leaf Mold symptoms: diffuse yellow chlorotic patches on the upper leaf surface, which corresponds to the fungal growth (Passalora fulva) visible on the underside of leaves.
